partial_design: Retain O_verify_voter_support and all five selected bindings. Build a package raft TestAssurance test with fixed voters L, V1, V2 and nonvoter N. Initialize the boundary fixture using the observed Raft fields, configuration storage, newSaturationMetric initialization and setupLeaderState, with actual followerReplication objects but no replication workers. Explicitly record manual initialization and omission of distributed startup as adaptations. Register the primary future through Raft.verifyLeader under exclusive ownership, observe registration, then synchronously call N's actual replication object's notifyAll(true). Independently derive contributor eligibility and majority from configured ServerID and Suffrage, including local voter L. Replace the cross-channel rendezvous with a second, separately identified verification registered after the primary contribution returns. Deliver V1's affirmative notification for this second verification. Any terminal notification already produced for the primary precedes the second verification's notification on the same buffered verifyCh. Start the actual leaderLoop only after these synchronous calls. Observe the second future's completion, then request shutdown and join leaderLoop independently of the primary outcome. Inspect the primary's completion and final state only after the join. Record whether V1 remained registered for the primary before delivering its notification: if so, V1 can change the primary's support, so this sequence must not be used as a nonvoter-only endpoint without separating the rendezvous from contribution delivery. The final harness must instead use a separately initialized control future queued directly on verifyCh as an explicitly declared processing-marker adaptation, or another source-grounded FIFO endpoint that cannot contribute to the primary. The marker must exercise only the existing completion branch and must never stand in for the primary observation. Include an independent permitted case with V1 support. Emit correlated registration, admitted contribution and independent result events using stable operation IDs. Compare actual primary success with independently counted voter support. Timeouts, missing completion markers or unsuccessful shutdown joins remain unknown. Preserve the distinction between internal future completion and public VerifyLeader execution. Distributed response reachability, freshness, membership transitions and stale reads remain unresolved; no new producer or filter is proposed.
